title: Planning a Home Addition in Westchester NY? Here's What You Need to Know
excerpt: Adding space to your Westchester home requires more than just a contractor. You need someone who understands local building codes, can design what you actually want, and won't disappear once the work starts.
content:
If you're thinking about adding space to your house in Westchester, you're not alone. Plenty of homeowners here choose to expand rather than move. But a home addition is different from regular renovation work. It touches zoning laws, lot lines, and building permits. It touches how your house looks and how it functions every day. That's why you need someone who can handle both the design and the construction.

Silvio M. Luca runs House Architecture & Construction out of Eastchester, and he's both a licensed architect in New York and a licensed general contractor. That matters. It means he's not handing your project off to someone else halfway through. He's there from the first sketch through the final inspection.

Why Design-Build Makes Sense for Home Additions

Most homeowners don't realize that a design-build approach in Westchester saves time and money. When your architect is also your contractor, decisions get made faster. Problems get solved before they become expensive. There's no blame game between two different companies.

In towns like Scarsdale and Bronxville, where homes are close together and lot lines matter, this matters even more. Your designer needs to understand what a contractor can actually build. Your contractor needs to understand what the architect's vision really is. When they're the same person, that conversation never breaks down.

Understanding Permits Across Westchester Towns

Every town in Westchester County has its own building department. That's just how it works. Whether you're in White Plains, Larchmont, Tarrytown, or Pelham, you'll be pulling permits locally. The standards are similar, but the processes vary slightly from town to town.

Having someone who knows how each municipality works matters. Silvio handles the permit process for homeowners throughout Westchester, including smaller communities like Tuckahoe and Hastings-on-Hudson. He knows what each building department wants to see before you even submit the application.

Second Stories, Primary Suites, and More

A home addition in Westchester isn't one-size-fits-all. Some people need a second story because their lot won't allow them to expand sideways. Others want a primary suite addition with a walk-in closet and spa bathroom. Some families need a new kitchen that opens into the living space.

Whether you're working in Harrison, New Rochelle, Rye, or any other part of Westchester, the project scope changes everything. A residential architect in Scarsdale might design an addition very differently than one in Ardsley or Dobbs Ferry, based on what the lot allows and what the neighborhood looks like. That's where experience in your specific town actually helps.

Silvio doesn't specialize in just one service or just one town. He's built additions, kitchens, bathrooms, and custom homes throughout Westchester County. He takes on historic restorations and open-concept conversions too. Each project is different because each house and each family is different.
